operating_notes.text: The Enforcement Directorate released all of Dalmia Cement (Bharat)'s attached land parcels on 21 April 2026 against a ₹92.52 Cr bank guarantee, with the alleged proceeds of crime cut from ₹793.34 Cr to ₹92.52 Cr.
FY26 other expenses rose only 1.5% to ₹8,489 Cr while revenue grew 5.9%, helping EBITDA margin reach 20.83%.
FY26 capex fell 22.8% to ₹2,056 Cr, with CWIP of ₹2,593 Cr at March 2026.
DCBL's ₹93 Cr bank guarantee released all ED-attached land parcels on 21 April 2026, cutting alleged proceeds of crime from ₹793 Cr.
FY26 sales volume 30.0 MnT (+2%); Q4 volume 8.8 MnT, with the Rajgangpur breakdown cutting Q4 growth by ~3%.
FY26 EBITDA per tonne ₹1,027 vs ₹820 in FY25; Q4FY26 ₹1,023, up ₹260/t QoQ after adjusting for a ₹46 Cr one-off incentive in Q3.
Cement capacity 49.5 MnTPA rising to 55.5 MnTPA in FY27 (Belgaum, Pune) and 61.5 MnTPA in Q2-Q3 FY28 (Kadapa); project capex ~₹3.2K Cr in the last two years and ~₹2.2K Cr expected in FY27.
DCBL to hold 41% (26% fully diluted) of Oyster Green Hybrid Five, an SPV with 21.6 MW wind and 14 MWp solar, for captive power to the Kadapa plant; ₹17.35 Cr for 1,73,50,000 shares at ₹10 par.
Q4FY26 sales volume 8.8 MT (+3% YoY); a March breakdown cost about 1.5 lakh tons of clinker and 300,000 tons of cement.
Q4FY26 EBITDA per ton ₹1,023 vs reported Q3 ₹823; adjusted for the ₹46 Cr one-off incentive, up ₹260/t QoQ.
Petcoke prices at about $160/t; every 5% diesel price rise adds about ₹15/t to freight cost.

Acquired assets: Rewa integrated (1.1 MnTPA cement, 3.3 MnTPA clinker, 62 MW thermal, 100+ MnT limestone reserves), Chunar grinding (2.5 MnTPA, 37 MW), Churk grinding (1.0 MnTPA), Sadwa blending (0.6 MnTPA).
Further debottlenecking/brownfield potential of 0.5-0.7 MnTPA clinker and 1.5-2.0 MnTPA cement at the acquired sites.
Existing capacity utilisation 61% on a pro-rata basis.
Completed acquisition of JP Associates cement undertaking with 5.2 MnTPA cement and 3.3 MnTPA clinker capacity, bringing total capacity to 54.7 MnTPA.
Premium products reached 25% of the portfolio in Q1FY27, and the Weather365 premium-plus offering was launched during the quarter.
Incentive accrual was ₹45 Cr in the quarter against ₹60 Cr collected, leaving ₹822 Cr outstanding; accrual guided at ₹45-50 Cr per quarter for the next couple of years.
Blended fuel cost rose QoQ from ₹1.36 to ₹1.47 per Kcal, and 48% of power consumption came from renewable energy.

timeline.summary: On 22 April 2026 Dalmia Bharat said the Enforcement Directorate had, by order dated 21 April 2026, released all of Dalmia Cement (Bharat)'s attached land parcels against a ₹92.52 Cr bank guarantee, cutting the alleged proceeds of crime from ₹793.34 Cr to ₹92.52 Cr, which DCBL is still appealing.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹4,245 Cr (+3.8% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹387 Cr (-11.0% YoY).
On 28 April 2026 Dalmia Bharat's Q4 & FY26 earnings release showed FY26 revenue ₹14,804 Cr (+5.9%); EBITDA ₹3,083 Cr (+28%) and PAT ₹1,157 Cr (+65%)

On 29 April 2026 Dalmia Cement (Bharat) agreed to buy 41% (26% fully diluted) of Oyster Green Hybrid Five, an Oyster Renewable SPV with 21.6 MW wind and 14 MWp solar, for ₹17.35 Cr to supply captive power to its Kadapa plant, subject to conditions precedent and expected within four months.
On 1 May 2026 Dalmia Bharat filed the transcript of its 28 April 2026 Q4FY26 call, guiding FY27 capex of ₹3,200-3,400 Cr and flagging a ₹125-150/t cost rise in Q1FY27.
On April 30, 2026, DCBL received an order from the Additional Commissioner of CGST (Appeals) waiving a ₹12 lakh penalty for FY18 ITC.

On 8 May 2026, Dalmia Bharat clarified via exchange disclosure that media reports concerning an SFIO report on mutual fund units are speculative and that funds were released by the Supreme Court in 2019.

On 21 May 2026, Dalmia Cement (Bharat) signed a Business Transfer Agreement with Jaiprakash Associates and Adani Infra to acquire 5.2 MnTPA cement and 3.3 MnTPA clinker capacity in Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh for ₹2,850 Cr, lifting Dalmia Bharat's cement capacity to 54.7 MnTPA on consummation.

On 23 May 2026, Dalmia Bharat's board called the 13th AGM for 30 June 2026, sought a special resolution for securities issuance up to ₹4,000 Cr, recommended Walker Chandiok & Co LLP's re-appointment as auditor for a second five-year term, and fixed 23 June 2026 as record date for the ₹5/share FY26 final dividend.
On May 29, 2026, Dalmia Cement completed the acquisition of 5.2 MnTPA cement and 3.3 MnTPA clinker capacity from Jaiprakash Associates, taking total capacity to 54.7 MnTPA.
Y.H. Dalmia and 67 related entities declared no encumbrance on Dalmia Bharat shares as of March 31, 2026, under SEBI’s Regulation 31(4).
2026-10-21: Dalmia Bharat shareholders approved MD remuneration resolutions via postal ballot
